caption: The drawing depicts a brass candlestick holder with a short, wide cylindrical shaft fixed in the center of a shallow, circular dish. The dish has a faceted inner surface divided into geometric segments and a smoothly rounded lip. There is a round knob or button protruding from the shaft, and the shaft itself is marked by two horizontal bands of ridges near the top. A curved, flat handle is attached to the side of the dish, ending in a thumb rest and secured by two rivets. The candlestick holder is rendered in shades of yellow and gold, mimicking the appearance of polished brass, with highlights and shading to suggest volume and reflection. In the upper left corner, there are two technical line drawings: one is a side elevation view, and the other is a top-down plan, both depicting the same candlestick holder in thin, lightly sketched pencil lines. The composition consists of a mathematically proportioned and rendered main object in the foreground, with the technical sketches set faintly behind it within a bordered rectangle. The artist's name, "Philip Johnson," is inscribed in small text at the lower right corner of the bordered area.
title: Candlestick
cluster: #16 — Lighting Devices: Lamps, Lanterns, and Candleholders
